findings.body:
**Reviewer note:** I am Claude (Anthropic), not a GPT-tier model, so this is not a cross-family perspective. Only the spec and three context docs were inlined, so the spec's claims about `write-trace.mjs`, the pre-commit hook, the endpoint and the executor are unverified.

## Verdict: MINOR ISSUES (three DESIGN findings)

**1. DESIGN — Tier 1 has no named reader for the findings (§Every development tier).**
The spec makes "the side-effects reviewer" assess the advisory. `signal-vs-authority.md` says a second-pass reviewer runs only "for high-risk changes". For a small fix, the only reader I can see is the author, which is the gap the spec set out to close. Resolution: name who assesses findings at Tier 1, or state plainly that it is author self-assessment and record it as such.

**2. DESIGN — The review runs after the reviewer it feeds (same section).**
The advisory is generated inside `write-trace`, which "follows the second pass". Every non-empty report therefore triggers the reassess-and-refresh path. A refresh re-invokes a nondeterministic reviewer, which can produce different findings on identical input, so the loop has no stated end. Resolution: run the advisory as a step before the side-effects review and have `write-trace` only record it. Reuse the stored report when the input SHA is unchanged, and exclude the trace file from the hashed input so staging the trace does not make it stale.

**3. DESIGN — The pinned constitution has no drift detector (§Governing context; Purpose Rules 2 and 4; Rule 119).**
The vendored copies only change by explicit update, and the spec forbids a recurring monitor. Reporting the hash shows what was used, not that upstream has moved, so reviews can grade against superseded text indefinitely. Resolution: have the existing Rule 119 pull-request and daily checks flag a vendored commit that is behind upstream, and put the pin's age in every report.

**4. PRECISION — Size and noise are unquantified.**
The pair is long (123 rules, 79 of them "needs building"), and the spec gives neither the reviewer's input allowance nor the pair's size. `input-too-large` could be common on exactly the larger changes. Grading every one-line fix against the whole book also risks routine noise that builders learn to ignore. State the budget, and record what happened to each finding so the acted-on rate is measurable (Rule 39).

**5. PRECISION — The purpose document is marked "draft, awaiting approval".**
The spec calls the pair "governing" without mentioning this. Reports should carry the source's status line.

**6. PRECISION — Executor prompt dilution (§Automated executor).**
Adding both full books to the safety reviewer's prompt may weaken its safety focus. The alternative of passing the conformance report in as a signal is not discussed.

**7. PRECISION — Wider egress of diffs.**
Every Tier-1 diff now goes to the model provider. §Team posture says no new surface, but this is wider use of the existing one. Say whether secrets are scrubbed before sending.

**What holds up:** the advisory-only posture, the rule that an empty report is never approval, the single bounded attempt and the offline pinned assets are sound. I see no over-reliance on LLM authority, and no existing library or protocol would do this better.
